4 اشطأ ; (S, Msb;) or ↓ شَطَأَ , aor.
شَطَاَ , inf. n. شَطْءٌ and شُطُوْءٌ; (K;) or both; (TA;) It put forth its شَطْء [or sprouts, &c.]; (S, K;) syn. فَرَّخَ; (Msb;) said of seed-produce; (S, Msb, K;) and in like manner said of palm-trees (نَخْل); and the former verb, said of trees (شَجَر), they put forth sprouts around their bases, or stems. (K.) And اشطأت الشَّجَرَةُ بِغُصُونِهَا The tree put forth its branches. (TA.) ―
-b2- And the former verb, (assumed tropical:) He (a man) had a son who had attained to manhood and become like him; (AHn, K;) like أَصْحَبَ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
